policy: All author files are preserved byte-for-byte. The runner loads selected definitions by AST to prevent import-time training and exposes the same globals.
allowed_changes: Replace the author word-to-ID encoder with a reversible byte-tokenizer adapter.
Reserve seven shared special/structure IDs and resize only the input embedding and output projection dimensions.

Construct the model from the author's GPT class with the same d_model, d_ff, heads, layers, scientific-action limit, Adam learning rate, batch size, epochs, clipping, sampling, reward, and PINN settings.
Fix the author's empty Left assignment in the copied execution wrapper; the source file itself is unchanged.
Pass Delete_equation_name to read_dataset, because the published call site otherwise does not remove the held-out target.
Bind the optimizer to the model that is actually fine-tuned in the five-step reward continuation; the upstream variable is otherwise a new unoptimized model.
Use explicit run directories and deterministic seeds; record all hashes and parameters.
Extend only the positional embedding capacity identically for all arms, to fit the longest subword-expanded sequence; retain the author GRE generation-length condition.
Encode exact original GRE spellings at semantic action boundaries and score complete prefix-free codewords before invoking the original author GPT.step. No LaTeX conversion or action-space expansion.
Keep published EOS placement in data augmentation; all arms encode exactly the same GRE sequences.
For disk Poisson, fix the author get_meta four-value unpack of a function returning two values. No numerical derivative or reward changes.
Record numerical PINN failures without resampling or substituting another candidate; retain outcomes in result denominators.
Instrument common data sampling hashes, model state hashes, parameter/optimizer binding, timing, and checkpoint reload without changing the loss or update equations.
forbidden_changes: No change to transformer block equations, width, depth, attention, activation, loss, data augmentation semantics, reward formula, candidate selection, or PINN objective.
No pretrained GPT-2 weights; all three author-architecture models start from new random weights.
No tokenizer-specific training examples or target-specific token reservations.
